explanation: The Charter gave the convention both its machinery and its authority. The General Assembly resolved in December 1946 that genocide was a crime under international law, the Economic and Social Council had the text drafted, and the Assembly adopted it two years later. The claim is narrow on purpose. This atlas will hold a good many United Nations instruments, and that the United Nations convened the conference is no argument on its own about any of them. Here it is one because the convention is the first treaty made out of the Charter’s human-rights clauses, and the precedent for the ones that followed.
